summary: Midea or Mideia (Ancient Greek: Μιδέα / Μιδεία) is, in this atlas entry, the Phrygian woman by whom Electryon of Mycenae begot the bastard Licymnius — mother of the sole surviving Electryonid line after the legitimate sons fell fighting the Taphians.
etymology: Ancient Greek Μιδέα / Μιδεία; also the name of Argive and Boeotian eponyms and a Danaid.

sections.heading: Mother of Licymnius
paragraphs: Apollodorus (Bibliotheca 2.4.5–6) records that after Electryon's legitimate sons by Anaxo he had also a bastard, Licymnius, by a Phrygian woman Midea. When the sons of Pterelaus and Electryon's legitimate brood slew one another, only young Licymnius survived — half-brother of Alcmena and uncle of Heracles.
Beyond that kinship the sources give her no further genealogy or episode.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: Other Mideias include a nymph mother of Aspledon, a Danaid who killed Antimachus, and an Argive eponym. The atlas id midea-phrygian is Electryon's Phrygian consort alone.
